steps.action: Push the heavy box together in the same direction until it parks on TEAM; then hop past it.
steps.expected_feedback: The box requires both pushers and its weight activates TEAM, opening the shared door.
steps.observed_feedback: The ordinary attempt moves both heroes through the team area and continues without death.

common_mistakes.mistake: Only one hero pushes the heavy box or the box is left short of TEAM.
common_mistakes.consequence: A heavy box does not move with one pusher; if it does not reach TEAM, the shared door stays closed.
common_mistakes.recovery: Reposition both players behind the box and push together toward the pad; the ordinary route shows the box area is on the broad starting floor.

confidence_reason: Source defines the crate, pads, ferry, slime and exits, and a fresh ordinary-input route reaches both exits with zero deaths. Recovery after falling and human discovery remain unobserved.

confirmed: The title/subtitle and screenshot correctly suggested a team-operated cargo/ferry problem with a central gap and matching exits.
The lower route includes a meaningful physical hazard: the slime below the ferry is lethal.
missed_mechanics: The cargo is a heavy box requiring two heroes pushing together; once on the x2 TEAM pad it contributes weight 2 and opens the team door.
Isp must hold STOP to brake/power the ferry and open Pac’s landing gate; Pac reaches a latching RESCUE that keeps power and opens Isp’s finish gate.
The route requires crossing a lethal slime gap on the ferry, with separate safe banks.
Two optional role-owned collectibles are present.
incorrect_inferences: The first pass hypothesized that a team pad might require both heroes to stand on it simultaneously. Actual source shows the heavy box itself supplies weight 2 once parked; both heroes are needed to push it, not to remain on the pad.
The first-pass prior ledger misattributed level_04’s pad roles. Level_04 actually teaches Pac STEADY and Isp RESCUE; this paired record corrects the earlier note without altering the first pass.
changed_judgments: Reasoning stays at 3: actual route confirms an ordered cargo/STOP/RESCUE plan, but the first-pass 3 was an inference from the team labels and gap.
Cooperation rises from 3 to 4 because two heroes must jointly move the heavy crate and later perform distinct STOP/RESCUE roles.
Execution rises from 2 to 3 because both must coordinate crate movement and traverse a ferry gap over lethal slime.
Timing changes from null to 1: ferry movement and Isp’s stop role matter, but stopping and the latched rescue allow a readable, repeatable sequence.
Hazards changes from null to 2 because slime is lethal beneath the mandatory ferry crossing, though the approach and ferry are safe surfaces.
Novelty rises from 2 to 3 because cargo parking, ferry role controls and a two-player heavy push are recombined in one dependent route.
Recovery cost changes from null to 2: a misplaced team cargo or early STOP release repeats setup, while actual fall/death recovery was not directly exercised.
Solution clarity stays at 2: labels name the key objects but do not fully state that two players must push the heavy box or why rescue must follow stop.
unresolved: The native trace establishes one successful route, not how often humans misplace the box or fall from the ferry.
No failed attempt directly establishes post-death recovery cost.
Human first-time understanding, co-op communication, enjoyment and route preference remain unmeasured.

single_operator_note: One operator must push the heavy box with both heroes at once, then separately hold Isp on STOP while moving Pac across, before switching to Isp. The paired key groups make the simultaneous push possible but raise attention and sequencing demands outside the two-human baseline.
